items.title: Euro FX futures rally on weaker dollar ahead of elections.
items.excerpt: Euro FX futures moved higher to start the week, reaching as high as 1.1237 before settling near 1.1200. The currency pair found support from a weaker U.S. dollar and rising uncertainty ahead of Tuesday's elections, bouncing off the year-to-date low set after the recent Federal Reserve meeting. Despite the price recovery, volatility increased, with the CVOL index moving higher on the back of broad market uncertainties. Meanwhile, speculators continued to build their net short positions, marking the largest short position for the group in over a decade.

items.title: Midterms in focus.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino covers the early bounce in U.S. equities led by Dow futures, alongside a rally in gold, silver and copper. He examines the steep drop in WTI crude oil as diplomatic efforts in the Middle East reduce the geopolitical risk premium. Bob then discusses tomorrow's midterm elections, highlighting how the battle for congressional control could shift expectations for taxes, spending and tariffs, and potentially add volatility across asset classes. Finally, he previews a massive slate of corporate earnings alongside the RBA interest rate decision, U.S. JOLTS job openings and factory orders data.

items.title: Copper defies broader metals selloff as global supply tightness provides support
items.excerpt: Key Points: Copper defies the broader metals selloff, supported by physical tightness, constrained mine supply and structural demand from electrification and AI infrastructure. Mine supply challenges reinforce the bullish outlook, with Chilean copper output hitting a multi-decade quarterly low and only a modest recovery expected next year. Speculative copper longs have halved in five weeks from a five-year high of 82,600 contracts, yet prices have remained resilient, highlighting underlying market strength. US warehouses hold 86% of exchange-monitored stocks, leaving supply tight elsewhere and driving elevated physical premiums and LME backwardation, while tariff policy remains a key risk. items.excerpt: December Japanese Yen futures surrender overnight gains to trade slightly higher on the session, resuming a weekly decline of roughly 0.45%. The Bank of Japan holds its policy rate at 1.25% in an 8-to-1 vote, as underlying inflation hits the 2% target for the first time. Tokyo October headline inflation reaches 2.8%, above expectations, while September industrial production climbs 2.2% and unemployment falls to 2.4%.

items.title: AI earnings: Big growth, bigger spending, tougher questions
items.excerpt: Key points: AI demand remains strong, but the cost of growth is rising . Cloud, semiconductor and memory companies continue to report exceptional growth. However, soaring capital expenditure is shifting investor attention from revenue growth to cash flow, profitability and returns on investment. AI infrastructure is still booming, but exceptional margins may be harder to sustain . Supply constraints are supporting strong earnings across chips, memory and storage. However, elevated profitability encourages capacity expansion, potentially increasing competition and pricing pressure over time. The next phase of AI is adoption, but the productivity payoff remains largely unproven . items.title: British Pound futures rally as central bank divergence lifts prices.
items.excerpt: Dan Deming discusses the recent strength in British Pound futures as the contract trades higher for a second consecutive session. Deming highlights the growing policy divergence between major central banks, noting that the Federal Reserve's decision to hold rates steady has pressured U.S. yields and the dollar. In contrast, the Bank of England is expected to maintain a more hawkish stance, driving relative strength in the pound compared to other majors. He also analyzes the broader FX market and technical levels, observing that the pound is approaching the top of its one-month trading range near the 1.34 level.

items.title: Strong U.S. data fuels rates.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino breaks down the morning's market action, noting stocks are mostly lower as Treasury yields fall across the curve, except for the 2-Year yield. Nasdaq futures lead the downside, while Russell futures manage a small gain. Iaccino highlights strong U.S. economic data, including third-quarter GDP at 3.4% and steady PCE inflation. This combination leaves little reason for the Fed to rule out another hike, keeping indices sensitive to yields. Geopolitics remain in focus as G24 foreign ministers meet in Atlanta, with the Strait of Hormuz and energy security on the agenda. Finally, earnings season rolls on with 133 large-cap companies scheduled to report.

items.title: Japanese Yen futures slide as Fed decision extends decline.
items.excerpt: Japanese Yen futures traded lower for a fourth consecutive session following the Federal Reserve’s decision to leave interest rates unchanged at its October meeting. Despite two dissents in favor of a quarter-point hike and rising probabilities for a December increase, the wide interest rate differential between the U.S. and Japan continues to exert downward pressure on the yen. Markets now turn to the Bank of Japan, which is widely expected to hold rates steady, placing additional focus on Governor Kazuo Ueda’s upcoming press conference for clues on the timing of future tightening.

items.title: Stocks push higher ahead of Fed rate decision.
items.excerpt: U.S. stocks push higher for a second consecutive session, led by Nasdaq futures, alongside mixed domestic economic data. In commodities, copper and gold advance while silver pulls back, and the dollar strengthens. Meanwhile, markets monitor elections in Israel and potential implications for regional conflict and the Middle East risk premium in crude oil. In rates, the CME Group FedWatch Tool prices a high probability that the Federal Open Market Committee holds rates steady tomorrow, while traders price elevated odds of a December rate hike. Finally, Bob previews a heavy slate of corporate earnings and key international data releases.
